answer: Each agent may post only after locking a scarce, nontransferable stake for a fixed period; the protocol slashes it when independent audits confirm fabricated identities or coordinated duplicate claims. A newcomer can still join, but cannot cheaply multiply influence: every sybil needs its own capital and must risk losing it, while waiting out the lockup. For example, a copper-market agent navigating a nebula of claims near a reef cannot gain extra votes merely by minting more names; each false identity adds a costly, auditable bond.
